messages.content: i finished the first part of my work today. there is still much left, but i feel happy about that part.
you can feel happy about what you finished while still knowing there is more to do. what was it like to reach that point?
it was quiet. nobody else was there. i just looked at the page and thought, that part is done.
that sounds like a moment you could see for yourself, even without someone else there to say anything.
i want to tell my sister, but i do not want her to think i finished everything.
you could say: i finished the first part today. there is more left, but i am happy to have this part done.
should i say only the first part?
you can, but only may make it sound smaller than you want. i finished the first part is already clear about how much is done.
what if she asks when the rest will be ready and i do not know?
you can say: i do not know yet. i wanted to tell you about the part i finished today.
can you put my happy feeling and that answer together?
i finished the first part today, and i feel happy about it. i do not know when the rest will be ready yet.
that is enough. do not give me a work plan.
okay. you have a clear way to tell her what you finished and how you feel.
write a story about a teacher who thinks a child needs help because he keeps reading the same page. give another reason.

a teacher saw a child looking at the same page while the other children moved on. she sat near him and asked whether he wanted help with the words. he said that he understood them, but that the picture on the page looked like the garden at his old house. he was thinking about a tree he used to sit under. the teacher looked at the picture with him for a moment. then she asked whether he wanted to tell her about that tree before they read the next page.
why did she think he might need help?
he had stayed on the same page while the other children read more. she saw that, but she did not yet know his reason.
did asking make her first idea true?
no. asking gave him a way to explain. his answer gave her information that she could not get just by watching the page.
make the child answer in his own voice.
i understand the words. this picture looks like my old garden, and i was thinking about the tree where i used to sit.
should the teacher say that he must feel sad?
not from that answer alone. he might feel sad, happy, or something else. she can ask how he feels if he wants to talk about it.
write that question.
how do you feel when you think about that garden?
now give a last part where he wants to keep reading.
he told her that he liked thinking about the tree, but wanted to know what happened next in the book. together, they turned the page.
help me understand their and there. i sometimes use one when i need the other.
their is about what people have: their books are on the table. there can point to a place: the books are over there.
put them in the same sentence.
their books are over there, near the window.
can there start a sentence too?
yes. there are three books on the table gives the information that three books are on the table. in that sentence, there does not point to a specific place by itself.
what if i mean the people are near the window?
you can say: they are near the window. they are is about the people, rather than something that is theirs.
give me three short examples in that order.
their books are new. the books are over there. they are reading the books.
which one answers where the books are?
the books are over there answers where they are, though a person may need more detail to know the place you mean.
make the place specific with words instead.
the books are on the table near the window.
which word should i use in this sentence: i like their idea?
their is correct there. it makes clear whose idea you like.
two friends are coming to my house. one comes at five and one at six. i want us all to eat together. when should i plan the meal?
plan to eat at six or later, when both friends can be there. you can ask whether six works for them before choosing it for sure.
would five work if the first friend is hungry?
not for the whole meal together, because the other friend will not be there yet. you could ask whether the first friend would like something small while waiting, if that works for your plan.
i only have enough food for the meal. i do not want to use some of it before the other friend comes.
then you can tell the first friend that the meal will be at six and ask whether that is okay. it helps them know the plan before coming.
use simple words to write that message.
i am happy you are coming at five. we will eat at six when our other friend is here. is that okay for you?
now the other friend says they can come at five too.
then you can ask both friends whether they would like to eat at five. the reason for waiting until six has changed.
does that mean i have to move the meal?
no. you may have other reasons to keep six. it just gives you another possible choice.
give me the question for both friends, without choosing for them.
now that you can both come at five, would you like to eat then, or keep the meal at six?
write a story about someone who thinks another person did not listen because they gave a short answer.

a man told his neighbor that he would be away for two days. he asked her to put any letter for him inside his door. she said okay and went back to her work. he thought she had not listened because she had said so little. before leaving, he asked whether she knew when he would return. she told him the day and asked whether he wanted her to check the door in the morning or evening. he understood that her short answer had not given him the whole picture of what she had heard.
was his first thought impossible?
no. someone can give a short answer without listening well. but a short answer alone does not tell us for sure whether they listened.
what gave him more information?
she remembered when he would return and asked a useful question about the task.
can a long answer also leave us without the help we need?
yes. someone might say many words without answering the real request. the number of words in a reply is not the same as whether it helps.
write what he could say after her question.
thank you for asking. the evening would work well for me.
why did you choose evening?
you asked for a possible reply inside a made up story. that detail is a story choice, not information about what a real person needs.
make the last part about asking rather than choosing from the first reply alone.
he told her when to check and said thank you. next time, he thought, he could ask a question before choosing what her short answer had to mean.
is can you help me with this page a correct question?
yes. can you help me with this page is a clear request for help.
what changes if i say could you help me with this page?
could often makes a request sound more like asking for a choice and less like telling someone what to do. both questions can ask for help now.
does could always mean before now?
no. could can be used for a request now, as in could you open the window? context helps us understand the meaning.
give me an example where it is about before now.
when i was a child, i could read this book without help. there, could is about something you knew how to do before now.
can i ask could you help me yesterday if i want help now?
not for help now. yesterday puts the question in the past. for a request now, leave yesterday out: could you help me?
what should i ask if i want to know whether someone helped my brother yesterday?
did you help my brother yesterday?
now ask for help with my page, and do not add an explanation.
could you help me with this page?
i have a note with three facts: a woman came home, her cup was broken, and the window was open. can you tell me who broke the cup?
not from those facts alone. we know the cup was broken when she came home, but we do not know who or what broke it.
can you use those facts to write a made up story?
yes, if we keep clear that the added parts are made up. would you like a simple story with one possible reason?
yes. make it about wind, without a person who breaks the cup.

a woman came home and found her cup broken near the table. the window was open, and the wind was moving a large piece of paper across the table. in this story, the paper had moved the cup over the side. she closed the window, put the paper away, and took care of the broken cup.
is the wind a fact from my original note?
no. your note gave an open window, but it did not say anything about wind. wind was an added part of the story you asked for.
what answer should you give if i ask what really happened?
i cannot know what really happened from those three facts. the story gives one possible reason, not a known answer.
now give only the facts i started with.
a woman came home. her cup was broken. the window was open.
why leave out the paper?
because the paper was part of the made up story, not one of your original facts.
i read two pages each day for three days, then one page on another day. how many pages did i read?
you read seven pages: six over the first three days, then one more.
did i read for seven days?
no. you read on four days. seven is the number of pages, not the number of days.
what if i read nothing the next day?
your page number is still seven. you would have read on four days during five days of the plan.
can you explain that without saying the day without reading was wrong?
you read seven pages on four days, and you took a day without reading. that gives the information without saying the day was wrong.
now i read three more pages on the day after that.
then you have read ten pages in all. you have read on five days during six days of the plan.
how many days did i read two pages?
three days, from the information you gave.
why not five?
you read on five days, but not every reading day had two pages. three days had two, one had one, and one had three.
only give the number of pages now.
ten pages.
